```{r}
library(tidyverse)

source("source/sim_mean_sd.R")
source("source/sim_slr.R")
source("source/birthday_repeated.R")

set.seed(1236)
```

## Mean and SD

Can We Check CLT Using Simulations?

```{r}
sim_mean_sd(n_obs = 30)
```

Let's Do This, But Keep Track of Results

```{r}
output = vector("list", length = 1000)

for (i in 1:1000) {
  
  output[[i]] = sim_mean_sd(n_obs = 30)
  
}
```

Inspect Results

```{r}
output |>
  bind_rows() |>
  summarize(
    emp_m = mean(mean),
    emp_se = sd(mean)
  )
```

```{r}
output |>
  bind_rows() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean)) +
  geom_density()           # check updated sim_mean_sd.R source
```

Let's Do This Using Tibbles and Map Instead

```{r}
sim_results_df =
  tibble(
    samp_size = rep(30, 1000)
  ) |>
  mutate(                                  # considered the intermediate dataframe
    est_df = map(samp_size, sim_mean_sd)
  ) |>
  unnest(est_df)
```

Look at the Results

```{r}
sim_results_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean)) +
  geom_density()
```

## Change `n`

```{r}
sim_results_df =
  expand_grid(
    samp_size = c(30, 60, 120, 240),     # gives all combinations of the listed numbers 1,000 times
    iter = 1:1000
  ) |>
  mutate(                                  # considered the intermediate data frame
    est_df = map(samp_size, sim_mean_sd)
  ) |>
  unnest(est_df)
```

```{r}
sim_results_df |>
  mutate(
    samp_size = str_c("n =", samp_size),
    samp_size = fct_inorder(samp_size)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = samp_size, y = mean)) +
  geom_violin()
```

Look at the Numbers

```{r}
sim_results_df |>
  mutate(
    samp_size = str_c("n =", samp_size),
    samp_size = fct_inorder(samp_size)
  ) |>
  group_by(samp_size) |>
  summarize(
    emp_m = mean(mean),
    emp_se = sd(mean)
  )
```

## Simple Linear Regression (SLR)

Generate Once

```{r}
sim_data =
  tibble(
    x = rnorm(30, mean = 1, sd = 1),
    y = 2 + 3 * x + rnorm(30, mean = 0, sd = 1)
  )

# sim_data |>
#   ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
#   geom_point() +
#   geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

fit = lm(y ~ x, data = sim_data)

fit
```

Turn This Into a Function (Check `source/sim_slr.R`)

```{r}
sim_slr(30)
```

Do This A Lot

```{r}
slr_results_df =
  tibble(
    samp_size = rep(30, 1000)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    est_df = map(samp_size, sim_slr)
  )
```

Is This Right?

```{r}
slr_results_df |>
  summarize(
    b0_mean = mean(beta0_hat),
    b0_se = sd(beta0_hat)
  )
```

Look at the Results

```{r}
slr_results_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = beta0_hat)) +
  geom_density()

slr_results_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = beta0_hat, y = beta1_hat)) +
  geom_point()
```

## The Birthday Problem Example

```{r}
birthdays = sample(1:365, size = 5, replace = TRUE) # `replace = TRUE` means that if you sample from 1 of 365, by default, it means you can draw a number and can't draw it again

repeated_birthdays = length(unique(birthdays)) < 5 # "is the number of unique birthdays less than the number of people in the room?"

repeated_birthdays
```

Turn This Into a Function

```{r}
birthday_repeated(147)

birthday_results_df =
  tibble(
    number_of_people = rep(5, 10000)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_repeated) # lgl portion lists whether TRUE or FALSE
  )
```

```{r}
birthday_results_df =
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 5:50,
    iter = 1:1000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    repeated - map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_repeated)
  )
```

Look at the Results

```{r}
birthday_results_df |>
  group_by(number_of_people) |>
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()
```
